sp.p: That he all the time of his life which he lead in the Earth, but especially at the end1 Peter 2:4; 1 Peter 3:18; Isaiah 53:12 thereof, sustained the wrath of God, both in body and soul, against the sin of mankind, that he might by his passion, as the1 John 2:2; 1 John 4:10 only propitiatory sacrifice, deliver our body and soul from everlasting damnation, and purchase us the favour of God, righteousness, and everlasting life.

sp.speaker: Question 37:
sp.p: For what cause should he suffer under Pilate, as being his Judg?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That he being innocentLuke 23:14; John 19:4 and condemned before a civil JudgPsalm 69:4; Isaiah 53:4–5; 2 Corinthians 5:21; Galatians 3:13 might deliver us from the severe Judgment of God which remained for all men.

sp.speaker: Question 38:
sp.p: But is there any more in it, that he was fastened to the Cross, than if he had suffered any other kind of death?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: There is more: for by this I am assured that he took upon himself the curse which did ly on me; for the death of the CrossDeuteronomy 21:23; Galatians 3:13 was accursed of God.

sp.speaker: Question 39:
sp.p: Why was it necessary for Christ to humble himself unto death?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Because the Justice and Truth of God could byGenesis 2:17 no other means be satisfied for our sins, but by the very death of theHebrews 2:9,14–15; Philippians 2:8 Son of God.

sp.speaker: Question 40:
sp.p: To what end was he buried also?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That thereby he might manifest that heActs 13:29; Matthew 27:60; Luke 23:53; John 19:38 was dead indeed.

sp.speaker: Question 41:
sp.p: But since that Christ died for us, why must we also die?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Our death is not a satisfaction for our Sins, but the abolishing of Sin, and our passageJohn 5:24; 1 Philippians 23; Romans 7:24 into everlasting Life.

sp.speaker: Question 42:
sp.p: What other commodity receive we by the Death of Christ?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That by the virtue of his Death our old man is crucified, slain, andRomans 6:6 buried together with him, (figured out in holy Baptism) that henceforth evil lusts and desires mayRomans 6:12 not reign in us, but weRomans 12:1 may offer our selves unto him a Sacrifice of thanksgiving.

sp.speaker: Question 43:
sp.p: Why is there added, he descended into Hell?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That in my greatest pains and most grevious temptations I may support my self with this comfort, that my Lord Jesus ChristIsaiah 53:10; Matthew 27:46 hath delivered me (by the unspeakable distresses, torments and terrors of his Soul, into which he was plunged both before, and then especially when he hanged on the Cross) from the straits and torments of Hell.

sp.speaker: Question 44:
sp.p: What doth the Resurrection of Christ profit us?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: First, by his Resurrection he vanquished death, that he1 Corinthians 15:6; 1 Corinthians 5:4–6; Romans 4:25; 1 Peter 1:3,&c and 21 might make us partakers of that Righteousness which he had gotten us by his death. Again, we are nowRomans 6:4; Colossians 3:1,&c; Ephesians 2:5 also stirred up by his Power to a new Life. Lastly, the Resurrection of our head, Christ, is a1 Corinthians 15:12,&c; Romans 8:11 Pledg unto us of our glorious Resurrection.

sp.speaker: Question 45:
sp.p: How understand you that he ascended into Heaven?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That Christ, his Disciples looking on, wasActs 1:9; Mark 16:19; Luke 24:51 taken up from the Earth into Heaven, and yetHebrews 4:14; Hebrews 7:25; Hebrews 9:11; Romans 8:34; Ephesians 4:10; Colossians 3:1 still is there for our sakes, and will be until he come again to judge the quick andActs 1:11; Matthew 24:30 the dead.

sp.speaker: Question 46:
sp.p: Is not Christ with us then until the end of the World, as he hath promised?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Matthew 28:20; Matthew 26:11; John 16:18; John 17:11; Acts 3:21 Christ is true God, and true Man, and so according to his Manhood is not now on Earth, but according to his Godhead, his Majesty, his Grace, andJohn 14:17,&c; John 16:13; Ephesians 4:8 Spirit is at no time from us.

sp.speaker: Question 47:
sp.p: Are not by this means the two natures in Christ pulled assunder, if his Humanity be not wheresoever his Divinity is?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: No; for seeing his Divinity is incomprehensible, andActs 7:48,44; Acts 17:27; Jeremiah 23:23–24 every where present, it followeth necessarily that the same is without the bounds of his humane Nature which he took unto him, and yet is nevertheless in it,Colossians 2:9; Matthew 28:6 and abideth personally united to it.

sp.speaker: Question 48:
sp.p: What Fruit doth the Ascension of Christ into Heaven bring unto us?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: First that1 John 2:1–2; Romans 8:34 he maketh Intercession to his Father in Heaven for us; next that we have our Flesh in Heaven, that we may be confirmed thereby, as by a sure Pledge, that it shall come to passe that he who is our HeadJohn 14:2; John 20:17; Ephesians 2:6 will lift us up, his Members, unto him: thirdly, thatJohn 14:16; John 16:7; 2 Corinthians 5:5; he sendeth us his Spirit instead of a Pledge between him and us, by whose forcible working we seek after not earthly but heavenly things, where he himselfColossians 3:1; Philippians 3:20,&c is sitting at the Right-Hand of God.

sp.speaker: Question 49:
sp.p: Why is it further said, he sitteth at the Right-Hand of God?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Because Christ therefore is ascended into Heaven, toEphesians 1:20; Ephesians 5:23; Colossians 1:18 shew there that he is the Head of his Church, by whom the FatherMatthew 28:18; John 5:22 governeth all things.

sp.speaker: Question 50:
sp.p: What profit is this Glory of our Head Christ unto us?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: First, that through his Holy SpiritEphesians 4:16 he poureth upon us his Members heavenly Graces, then that he shieldeth andPsalm 2:9; Psalm 110:2; John 10:28; Ephesians 4:8 defendeth us by his Power against all our Enemies.

sp.speaker: Question 51:
sp.p: What Comfort hast thou by the coming of Christ again to judge the quick and the dead?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That in all my Miseries and Persecutions, I look with myLuke 21:28; Romans 8:23; Philippians 3:20; Titus 2:13 Head lifted up, for the very same who before yielded himself unto the Judgment of God for2 Thessalonians 1:6–7; 1 Thessalonians 4:16; Matthew 25:41 me, and took away all Malediction from me, to come Judge from Heaven to throw all his and my Enemies into everlasting Pains; but toMatthew 25:34 translate me with all his chosen unto himself, into Celestiall Joys, and everlasting Glory.

sp.speaker: Question 52:
sp.p: What believest thou concerning the Holy Ghost?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: First, that He is true and Coeternal God, with theGenesis 1:2; Isaiah 48:16; 1 Corinthians 3:16; 1 Corinthians 6:19; Acts 5:3–4 eternal Father, and the Son; secondly, that he isMatthew 28:19; 2 Corinthians 1:2 also given unto me, to makeGalatians 3:14; 1 Peter 1:2; 1 Corinthians 6:17 me, through a true Faith, Partaker of Christ and all his Benefits, toActs 9:31 comfort me, and toJohn 14:16; 1 Peter 4:14 abide with me for ever.

sp.speaker: Question 53:
sp.p: What believest thou concerning the Holy and Catholick Church of Christ?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: I believe that the Sonmissing of God doth frommissing the beginning of themissing World to the End thereof, gather,Isaiah 59:21; Ephesians 5:26 defend, and preserve unto himself by his SpiritActs 2:4,42; Ephesians 4:3–6 and Word, out ofMatthew 16:18 whole Mankind, a1 John 3:21; 2 Corinthians 13:5 Company chosen to everlasting Life, and agreeing in true Faith; and that I am a lively Member of that Company, and so shalmissing remain for ever.

sp.speaker: Question 54:
sp.p: What mean those words, The Communion of Saints?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: First, that all and every one who believeth, are in1 John 1:3; Romans 8:32; 1 Corinthians 1:2; 1 Corinthians 13:21; 1 Corinthians 6:17 common Partakers of Christ and all his Graces, as being his Members; and then that every one ought1 Corinthians 12:21; Philippians 2:4–6 readily and chearfully to bestow the Gifts and Graces which they have received to the common Commodity and Safety of all.

sp.speaker: Question 55:
sp.p: What believest thou concerning Remission of Sins?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That God, for the Satisfaction made by Christ,1 John 2:2; 2 Corinthians 5:19,21 hath put out all theJeremiah 31:34; Psalm 103:3–4; Psalm 10:11; Romans 7:24–25; Romans 8:1–3 Remembrance of my Sins, and also of that Corruption within me wherewith I must fight all my life time, and doth freely indow me with the Righteousness of Christ, that I come not at anyJohn 3:18 time into Judgment.

sp.speaker: Question 56:
sp.p: What Comfort hast thou by the Resurrection of the Flesh?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That not only my Soul, after it shall depart out of my Body, shallLuke 23:43; Philippians 1:23 presently be taken up to Christ, but that this my Flesh also, being raised up by the Power of Christ, shall be again united to my Soul, and1 Corinthians 15:53; Job 19:25–26; 1 John 3:2; Philippians 3:21 shall be made like to the glorious Body of Christ.

sp.speaker: Question 57:
sp.p: What Comfort takest thou of the Article of everlasting Life?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That forasmuch2 Corinthians 5:1–3 as I feel already in my Heart the beginning of everlasting Life,1 Corinthians 2:9; John 17:3 it shall at length come to pass that after this Life I shall enjoy full and perfect Bliss, wherein I may magnify God for ever, which Blessedness verily neither Eye hath seen, nor Ear heard, neither hath any Man in thought conceived it.

sp.speaker: Question 58:
sp.p: But when thou believest all these things, what profit redoundeth thence unto thee?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That I am righteous in Christ before God, and an HeirRomans 1:17; John 3:36; Romans 3:4,22,24–25,28; Romans 5:1; Galatians 2:16; Ephesians 2:8–9 of eternal Life.

sp.speaker: Question 59:
sp.p: How art thou righteous before God?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Only by Faith in Christ Jesus. So that although my Concience accuse me that I have grievously trespassed against all the Commandments of God, and have notRomans 3:9,&c kept one of them, and further am as yetRomans 7:23 prone to all Evil; yet notwithstanding ifRomans 3:22; John 3:18 I embrace these Benefits of Christ with a true Confidence and Perswasion of mind, the full andTitus 3:5; Ephesians 2:8–9 perfect Satisfaction, Righteousness and Holiness of Christ, without any1 John 2:2 Merit of Mine, of theRomans 3:24; Deuteronomy 9:5–6; Ezekiel 36:22 meer Mercy1 John 2:1,&c of God isRomans 4:4–5; 2 Corinthians 5:19 imputed and given unto me, and that so, as if neither I had committed any Sin, neither any Corruption did stick unto me; yea as if I my2 Corinthians 5:21 self had perfectly accomplished that Obedience which Christ accomplished for me.

sp.speaker: Question 60:
sp.p: Why affirmest thou that thou art made Righteous by Faith only?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Not for that I please God through the Worthiness of meer Faith, but because only the Satisfaction, Righteousness and Holiness of Christ is my Righteousness1 Corinthians 1:30,&c; 1 Corinthians 2:2 before God, and1 John 5:10 I cannot take hold of it, or apply it unto my self any other way than by Faith.

sp.speaker: Question 61:
sp.p: Why cannot our good Works be Righteousness, or some part of Righteousness before God?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Because that Righteousness which must stand fast before the Judgment of God, must be in all Points perfectGalatians 3:10; Deuteronomy 27:26 and agreeable to the Law of God. Now our Works, even the best of them, are imperfect in this Life, andIsaiah 64:6 defiled with Sin.

sp.speaker: Question 62:
sp.p: How is it that our good Works merit nothing, seeing God promiseth that he will give a Reward for them both in this Life, and in the Life to come?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That Reward is not given of merit,Luke 17:10 but of Grace.

sp.speaker: Question 63:
sp.p: But doth not this Doctrine make Men careless and profain?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: No, For neither can it be but they who are incorporated into Christ through Faith, should bring forth theMatthew 7:18; John 15:5 Fruits of Thankfulness.

sp.speaker: Question 64:
sp.p: Seeing then that only Faith maketh us Partakers of Christ and his Benefits, whence doth it proceed?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: From the Holy GhostEphesians 2:8; Ephesians 6:23; John 3:5; Philippians 1:29 who kindleth it in our Hearts by the preaching of the Gospel, and other Ordinances, andMatthew 28:19–20; 1 Peter 1:22–23 confirmeth it by the use of the Sacraments.

sp.speaker: Question 65:
sp.p: What are the Sacraments?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: They are sacred Signes, and Seals, set before our Eyes, and ordained of God for this cause, that he may declare and seal by them the Promise of his Gospel unto us, to wit, that he giveth freely Remission of Sins, andGenesis 17:11; Romans 4:11; Deuteronomy 30:6; Leviticus 6:25; Hebrews 9:8–9; Ezekiel 20:12; Isaiah 6:6–7; Isaiah 54:9–10 Life everlasting, not only to his all in general, but to every one in particular that believeth, for that only Sacrifice of Christ which he accomplished upon the Cross.

sp.speaker: Question 66:
sp.p: Doth then both the Word and Sacraments tend to that End, as to lead our Faith unto the Sacrifice of Christ finished on the Cross as to the only ground of our Salvation?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: It is even so; for the Holy Ghost teacheth us by the Gospel, and assureth us by the Sacraments, that the Salvation of all of us standeth in the only SacrificeRomans 6:3; Galatians 3:17 of Christ offered for us upon the Cross.

sp.speaker: Question 67:
sp.p: How many Sacraments hath Christ ordained in the new Testament?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Two; Baptism, and the Lord’s Supper.

sp.speaker: Question 68:
sp.p: What is Baptism?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Immersion or dipping of the Person in Water in the Name of the Father, Son, and Holy Ghost, by such who are duly qualified by Christ.Matthew 3:16; John 3:23; Acts 8:38–39; Romans 6:4

sp.speaker: Question 69:
sp.p: Who are the proper Subjects of this Ordinance?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Those who do actually profess Repentance towards God, Faith in, and Obedience to our Lord Jesus Christ.Acts 2:38; Acts 8:36–37

sp.speaker: Question 70:
sp.p: Are no Infants to be baptized?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: None by no means; for we have neither Precept nor Example for that Practice in all the Book of God.

sp.speaker: Question 71:
sp.p: Doth the Scripture any where expressly forbid the Baptizing of Infants?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: It is sufficient that the Divine Oracle commands the baptizing of Believers, unless we will make our selves wiser than what is written. Nadab and Abihu were not forbidden to offer strange Fire, yet for so doing they incurred God’s Wrath, because they were commanded to take Fire from the Altar.Matthew 28:18–19; Mark 16:16; Leviticus 9:24; Leviticus 10:16

sp.speaker: Question 72:
sp.p: May not the Infant Seed of Believers under the Gospel be baptized as well as the Infant Seed of Abraham under the Law was circumcised?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: No; For Abraham had a Command then from God to circumcise his Infant Seed, but Believers have no Command to baptise their Infants Seed under the Gospel.Genesis 17:9–12

sp.speaker: Question 73:
sp.p: Seeing the Infants of Believers are in the Covenant of Grace with their Parents, as some say, why may not they be baptized under the Gospel, as well as Abrahams Infant Seed was circumcised under the Law?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: By the Infants of Believers being in the Covenant of Grace, it must either be meant of the Covenant of Grace absolutely considered, and if so, then there is no total and final Apostacy of any Infant seed of Believers from the Covenant, but all must be saved then.Jeremiah 32:38–40; John 10:28 Or, 2. They must mean conditionally, on consideration that when they come to years of maturity, they by true Faith, Love, and Holiness of life, taking hold of God’s Covenant of Grace, shall have the Priviledges of it. This being their sence, I then demand what real spiritual priviledg the Infant-Seed of Believers, as such, have more than the Infant Seed of Unbelievers, if they live also to years of maturity, and by true Faith and Love take hold of God’s Covenant?Isaiah 56:3–8; Acts 10:34–35; John 3:16 I further demand, whether the Seal of the Covenant do not under those considerations belong as much to the Children of Unbelievers as to the Children of Believers? yea, and more too, under consideration the Infant Seed of the Unbeliever should take hold of God’s Covenant, and the Believers Infant-Seed do not; as often this is seen to the sorrow of many Godly Parents.Isaiah 56:3–8; Acts 10:34–35; John 3:16 3. Suppose all the Infant Seed of Believers absolutely in the Covenant of Grace; yet Believers under the Gospel ought no more to Baptise their Infant-Seed, than Lot to circumcise himself or his Infant-Seed, if he had had Males as well as Females, albeit nearly related to Abraham, yea, a Believer, and in the Covenant of Grace too: forasmuch as Circumcision was limited to Abraham and to his Family. Also by the same rule we may bring Infants to the Lord’s Table, forasmuch as the same qualifications are required to the due performance of Baptism, as there is to the Lord’s Supper.Acts 2:41–42 4. We must know the Covenant made with Abraham had two parts: first, a spiritual, which consisted in God’s promising to be a God toGenesis 17:19,21; Genesis 21:10; Galatians 4:30 Abraham, andActs 2:39; Romans 9:7–8,&c all his Spiritual-Seed in a peculiar manner, whether they were circumcised or uncircumcised, which believed as Abraham the Father of the Faithful did. And this was signified in God’s accepting such as his People which were not ofGalatians 3:16,28–29 Abrahams Seed, but bought with his Mony, and this Promise was sealed to Abraham by Circumcision, that through Jesus Christ (whom Isaac typified out) the Gentiles, the Uncircumcision which believed, should have their Faith counted for Righteousness, as Abrahams was before he was circumcised.Romans 4:9–14 2. This Promise consisted of temporal good: so God promised Abrahams Seed should injoy theGenesis 15:18; Genesis 17:8–11; Genesis 12:6–7; Genesis 13:15–17; Genesis 15:16 Land of Canaan, and have plenty of outward blessings, so sealed this Promise by Circumcision. It was also a distinguishing character of the Jews being God’s People from all the Nations of the Gentiles, which as yet were not the Seed of Abraham: but when the Gentiles came to believe, and by Faith became the People of God as well as the Jews, thenJohn 1:12; Romans 2:28–29; Philippians 3:3; Galatians 3:26–28 Circumcision, that distinguishing Mark, ceased; and the character of being the Children of God now, is Faith in Christ, and Circumcision of the Heart. So that whatever pretence there may be for the Infants of Believers to be Baptised first, as their being the Seed of Believers; or 2dly, their being in the Covenant; or 3dly, that the Infant-Seed of Abraham a Believer, was circumcised; all this you see avails nothing: for Circumcision was limited to such a Family, the Family of Abraham, all others, though Believers, were excluded; also limited to such a day, the eighth day, and what ever pretence might be made, it was not to be done before nor after; limited also to such a Sex, the Male, not the Female; which if Baptism came in the room of Circumcision, and is the Seal of the Covenant under the Gospel, as Circumcision was under the Law, none but the Males must be Baptised, because none but the Males were Circumciled; but as under the Law respecting Circumcision, so now under the Gospel respecting Baptism, it depends purely upon the will of the Law-giver, at what season, upon what Persons and terms Baptism is to be administred; unto which Prophet we shall all do well to hearken, Acts 3:22.

sp.speaker: Question 74:
sp.p: How art thou admonished and assured in Baptism, that thou art Partaker of the only Sacrifice of Christ?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Matthew 28:19; Acts 2:38 Because Christ commanded the outward washing of Water, adjoyningMark 16:16; Matthew 3:11; Romans 6:3 this Promise thereunto, that I am no less assuredly washed by his Blood and Spirit from the uncleanness of my Soul, that is, from all my Sins, than I amMark 1:4; Luke 3:3 washed outwardly with Water, whereby all the Filthiness of the Body useth to be purged.

sp.speaker: Question 75:
sp.p: What is it to be washed with the Blood and Spirit of Christ?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: It is to receive of God Forgiveness of Sins freely, for the Blood of Christ whichHebrews 12:24; 1 Peter 1:2; Revelation 1:5; Zechariah 13:1; Ezekiel 36:25,&c he shed for us in his Sacrifice upon the Cross; and also to be renewed by the Holy Ghost, and through his sanctifying of us to become Members of Christ, that we may more and more dy to Sin, andJohn 1:33; John 3:5; 1 Corinthians 5:11–13; Romans 6:4; Colossians 2:12 live holily and without blame.

sp.speaker: Question 76:
sp.p: Where doth Christ promise us that he will as certainly wash us with his Blood and Spirit, as we are washed with the Water of Baptism?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: In the Institution of Baptism, the words whereof are these,Matthew 28:19 Go, teach all Nations, baptising them in the Name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Ghost:Mark 16:16 he that shall believe, and be baptised, shall be saved; but he that will not believe, shall be damned. This Promise is repeated again when as the Scripture calleth Baptism the washing of the New-birth, and forgiveness of Sins.Titus 3:5 the washing of the New-birth, andActs 22:16 forgiveness of Sins.

sp.speaker: Question 77:
sp.p: Is then the outward Baptism of Water the washing away of Sins?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: It is not; for the1 Peter 3:21; Ephesians 5:25–26 Blood of Christ alone cleanseth us from1 John 1:7; 1 Corinthians 6:11 all Sin.

sp.speaker: Question 78:
sp.p: Why then doth the Holy Ghost call Baptism the washing of the New-birth, and forgiveness of Sins?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: God speaketh so not without great cause, to wit, not only to teach us that as the filth of our Body is purged by Water, so our Sins also areRevelation 1:5; Revelation 7:14; 1 Corinthians 6:11; purged by the Blood and Spirit of Christ, but much more to assure us by this divine Token and Pledg, that we are as verily washed from our Sins with the inward washing, as we areMark 16:16; Galatians 3:27 washed by the outward and visible Water.

sp.speaker: Question 79:
sp.p: What Principle of Christ’s Doctrine in the holy Scripture followeth Baptism in order?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Laying on of Hands, as in Hebrews 6:1–2

sp.speaker: Question 80:
sp.p: What is the form and end of this Ordinance?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Christ’s Ministers laying their hands solemnly upon the Head of the Baptised, with Prayer to Almighty God for an increase of the Graces2 Timothy 1:6; Acts 2:38–39 and Gifts of theJohn 14:16–18,26; John 16:7 Holy Ghost, to inable us to hold fast the Faith which we now visibly own, having entred into the Church by Holy Baptism, and also be helped thereby to maintain a constant War against theEphesians 1:13–14 World, Flesh, and the Devil.

sp.speaker: Question 81:
sp.p: Is it the Duty of every Christian to be under this Practice?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: It is so: And appeareth plainly, if we do first consider the Practice of the Primitive Saints, we may read in Acts 8:12–19, of Men and Women that were baptized by Philip in Samaria, which when the Church at Jerusalem heard thereof, they sent down St. Peter and St. John (two Apostles) to them, who when they came thither, laid their Hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost.Hebrews 5.1–2; Acts 7:38; Hebrews 1:2 What, them! some may say? were these they that were baptized which were Men and Women? So likewise in Acts 19:6–7. When Paul came to Ephesus he found certain Disciples there who were baptised, but had not heard whether there was any Holy Ghost, nor I conceive of the Promise of the Holy Ghost mentioned in Acts 1:4 then the Apostle layeth his Hands on them, and they received the Holy Ghost; and it is said the number of them was about twelve; and Reason sheweth us from this place, and Acts 8 where St. Peter and St. John laid hands on Men and Women, that had here bin twelve score, he would have laid his Hands on them all. And whereas ’tis objected, we do not find the three thousand in Acts 2 under this Ordinance, nor many others which were baptised. As to the three thousand ’tis plain enough they had bin taught it, and doubtless so practised this Ordinance, if we consider the Apostle writing to the Jews, in Hebrews 5 telleth them they had need be taught again the first Principles of the Oracles of God, of which Oracles, Laying on of Hands was one. And as for others which were baptised, where mention is not made of their being under this Ordinance, we may also say many hundreds were baptised which we have no mention of. Shall we conclude many of the Apostles were not baptised, because it is not particularly mentioned? so we must conclude the primitive Saints were not short in this point, although it be not always specified; forasmuch as it is called one of God’s Oracles, as we all know the Moral Law was, wch is perpetually binding, and universally obliging; also called aHebrews 5.1–2; Acts 7:38; Hebrews 1:2 Principle of Christs Doctrine, yea one of the first Principles; and that is not all, but called a foundation Principle, this with the other five must be laid first in that foundation, on which the Superstructure of Christianity must be built. And would it not have bin very unbecoming the Jews when God gave them ten Commandments, for them to have excluded the fourth? is it not also as unbecoming for any to exclude the fourth Principle of Laying on of Hands, a practical Principle of the Doctrine of Christ, and so practised by the Primitive Christians?

sp.speaker: Question 82:
sp.p: Did not the extraordinary Gifts of the Spirit follow upon laying on of Hands in the Apostles time?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: It did so: But not simply as the end of that Ordinance. For that Ordinance was appointed for the Ordinary Gifts of the Spirit to the Worlds end; though it is true, God honoured and crowned that Ordinance with Signes and Wonders in the primitive time, as he did others of his Appointment: as for instance, Acts 4 the Place was shaken, as the effect of the Churches Prayer; so Preaching was extraordinarily crowned when St. Peter converted three thousand at one Sermon; and in God’s giving the Holy Ghost to the House of Cornelius while Peter was preaching, so that they spake with Tongues, Acts 10. Also God crowned the holy Ordinance of Baptism extraordinarily, when the Spirit came in the likeness of a Dove, and sate upon our Saviour Christ as he came out of the Water, Matthew 3 and a Voice heard from Heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased. Also the Eunuch’s Baptism was wonderfully confirmed to him in God’s taking away Philip as soon as he came up out of the Water, insomuch that he went away rejoycing. Now, Beloved, as Prayer, Baptisme, Preaching, doth not cease, though it be not so miraculously owned as in the Primitive times; neither doth laying on of Hands cease, from the same Parity of Reason, though it be not so crowned now, as in the Apostles Days. Moreover our Brethren generally do hold, that five of those Principles in Hebrews 6 are the Duty of every individual Member to believe and practise, namely, every Member (say they) ought to repent, believe, be baptized, believe the Resurrection of the dead, and eternal Judgment; and why this of laying on of Hands should be excluded from being the Practice of every Christian, being a practical Ordinance, the bare belief of it not being enough, it being among the universal Principles of Christ’s Doctrine, I never yet did, nor cannot see any good Reason.

sp.speaker: Question 83:
sp.p: How art thou in the Lords Supper admonished and warranted that thou art Partaker of that only Sacrifice of Christ offered on the Cross, and of all his Benefits?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Because Christ hath commanded me and all the Faithful to eat of this Bread broken, and to drink of this Cup, distributed in Remembrance of him, with this PromiseMatthew 26:27–28; Mark 14:22–24; Luke 22:16,20; 1 Corinthians 10:16–17; 1 Corinthians 11:23–25; 1 Corinthians 12:13 adjoyned, first, that his Body was as certainly broken and offered for me upon the Cross, and his Blood shed for me, as I behold with my Eyes the Bread of the Lord broken unto me, and the Cup communicated unto me: and further, that my Soul is no less assuredly fed to everlasting life with his Body, which was crucified for me, and his Blood which was shed for me, than I receive and taste by the Mouth of my Body, the Bread and Wine, the Signs of the Body and Blood of our Lord, received at the Hand of the Minister.

sp.speaker: Question 84:
sp.p: What is it to eat the Body of Christ?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: It is not only to imbrace, by an assured Confidence of Mind, the whole Passion and Death of Christ, and thereby,John 6:35,40,47–48,50–51,53–54 to obtain Forgiveness of Sins, and everlasting Life, but also by the Holy Ghost, who dwelleth both in Christ, and us, so more and more toJohn 6:56 be united to his sacred Body, that though he beActs 3:21; Acts 1:9,&c; 1 Corinthians 11:26 in Heaven, and we on Earth, yet nevertheless we are Flesh of his Flesh, and Bone of hisEphesians 5:29–30,32; 1 Corinthians 6:15,17,19; 1 John 3:24; 1 John 4:13; John 14:23 Bones: and as all the Members of the Body are quickned by one Soul: so are we also quickned andJohn 6:56–58; John 15:1–6; Ephesians 4:15–16 guided by one and the same Spirit.

sp.speaker: Question 85:
sp.p: Where hath Christ promised that he will as certainly give his Body and Blood so to be eaten and drunken, as they eat this Bread broken, and drink this Cup?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: In the Institution of the Supper, the Words whereof are these.1 Corinthians 11:23,&c; Matthew 26:26,&c; Mark 14:22,&c; Luke 22:19 Our Lord Jesus Christ in the Night that he was betrayed, took Bread, and when he had given thanks, he brake it, and said, Take, eat, this is my Body which is broken for you: this do in Remembrance of me. Likewise also he took the Cup, when he had supped, andExodus 24:8; Hebrews 9:20 said, This Cup, is the new Testament in myExodus 13:9 Blood; this do as often as ye shall drink it in Remembrance of me: for as often as ye shall eat this Bread, and drink this Cup, ye shew the Lords Death till he come. This Promise, is repeated by St. Paul where he saith, The Cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the Communion of the Blood of Christ? the Bread which we break, is it not the Communion of the Body of1 Corinthians 10:16–17 Christ? for we that are many, are one Bread, and one Body, because we are all Partakers of one Bread.

sp.speaker: Question 86:
sp.p: Are then the Bread and Wine made the very Body and Blood of Christ?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: No, verily; but as the Water of Baptism is1 Corinthians 10:16–17; Matthew 26:28; Mark 14:24 not turned into the Blood of Christ, but is only a Signe and Pledge of those things that are sealed to us in Baptism; so neither is the Bread of the Lords Supper the very Body1 Corinthians 10:16,&c; 1 Corinthians 11:26,&c of Christ, although according to the manner of Sacraments, andGenesis 17:10,&c; Exodus 12:26–27,43,48; Exodus 13:9; Acts 7:8; Exodus 24:8; Leviticus 16:10; Leviticus 17:11; Isaiah 6:6–7; Titus 3:5; Acts 22:16; 1 Peter 3:21; 1 Corinthians 10:4 that Form of speaking of them which is usual unto the Holy Ghost, the Bread is called the Body of Christ.

sp.speaker: Question 87:
sp.p: Why then doth Christ call Bread his Body, and the Cup his Blood, or the new Testament in his Blood; and St. Paul calleth Bread and Wine the Communion of the Body and Blood of Christ?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Christ not without great Consideration speaketh so, to wit, not only for to teach us that as the Bread and Wine sustain the Life of the Body, so also his crucified Body, and Blood shed, are indeed the Meat and Drink of our Souls, whereby theyJohn 6:51,55–56 are nourished to eternal Life; but much more that by this visible Signe and Pledg, he may assure us that we are as verily Partakers of his Body and Blood, through the working of the1 Corinthians 10:16–17 Holy Ghost, as we do perceive by the Mouth of our Body, these holy Signes in Remembrance of him; and further also, that his Sufferings and Obedience is so certainly ours, as though we our selves had suffered Punishments for our Sins, and had satisfied God.

sp.speaker: Question 88:
sp.p: What Difference is there between the Supper of the Lord, and the Popish Mass?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: The Supper of the Lord testifieth unto us, that we have perfect Forgiveness of all our Sins, for that only Sacrifice of Christ, which himself onceHebrews 7:27; Hebrews 9:12,26,28; Hebrews 10:10,12,14; John 19:30; Matthew 26:28; Luke 22:19–20 fully wrought on the Cross; then also that we by Faith are grafted into1 Corinthians 6:17; 1 Corinthians 10:16; 1 Corinthians 12:13 Christ, who now according to his Human Nature is only in Heaven at the Right Hand ofHebrews 1:3,6,8,&c his Father, and there will beJohn 4:21–23; John 20:17; Luke 24:5; Acts 7:55–56; Colossians 3:1; Philippians 3:10; 1 Thessalonians 1:9–10 worshipped of us. But in the Mass it is denied that the quick and the dead have Remission of Sins, for the only Passion of Christ, except Christ also be daily offered for them by their Sacrificers: Further, also it is taught, that Christ is bodily under the Forms of Bread and Wine, and therefore is to be worshipped in them: and so the very Foundation of the Mass is nothing else but an utter denial of that only Sacrifice and Passion of Christ Jesus, and an accursed Idolatry.

sp.speaker: Question 89:
sp.p: Who are to come unto the Table of the Lord?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: They only, who are truly sorrowful they have offended God by their Sins, and yet trust that those Sins are pardoned them for Christ’s sake; and what other Infirmities they have, that those are covered by his Passion and Death; who also desire more and more to go forward in Faith and Integrity of life: but Hypocrites, and them which do not truly repent, do eat1 Corinthians 10:21; 1 Corinthians 11:28–29,&c and drink Damnation to themselves.

sp.speaker: Question 90:
sp.p: Are they also to be admitted to the Lords Supper who in Confession and Life declare themselves to be Infidels, profane, and ungodly?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: No; For by that means the Ordinance of God is profaned, and the Wrath of God is1 Corinthians 11:20,34; Isaiah 1:11,&c; Isaiah 66:3; Jeremiah 7:21,&c; Psalm 50:16,&c stirred up against the whole Assembly, wherefore the Church by the Commandment of Christ and his Apostles, inspired by the Holy Ghost, using the Keys of the Kingdom of Heaven, ought to drive them from this Supper till they shall repent and change their Manners.

sp.speaker: Question 91:
sp.p: How ought this Ordinance of the Lords Supper to be closed?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: In singing Praises to God vocally and audibly for his great Benefits and Blessings to his Church in the shedding of the most precious Blood of his Son to take away their Sin; which Blessings are pointed out in this Sacrament. Also we find our Lord and his Disciples did close up this Ordinance in singing an Hymn or Psalm; and if Christ did sing, who was going to dy, what cause have we to sing for whom he died, that we might not eternally dy, but live a spiritual and eternal life with Father, Son, and Spirit in unexpressible Glory.Matthew 26:30

sp.speaker: Question 92:
sp.p: You told us but now, that those who in Confession and Life declare themselves to be Infidels, profane and ungodly, should by the Keys of the Kingdom of Heaven be driven from this Supper: what are the Keys of the Kingdom of Heaven?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Preaching of the Gospel and Ecclesiastical Discipline, by which Heaven is opened to the Believers, andMatthew 16:19; Matthew 18:18 is shut against the Unbelievers.

sp.speaker: Question 93:
sp.p: How is the Kingdom of Heaven opened and shut by preaching of the Gospel?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: When by the Commandment of Christ it is publickly declared to all and every one of the Faithful, that all their Sins are pardoned them of God for the Merit of Christ, so often as they imbrace by a lively Faith the Promise of the Gospel: but contrarily is denounced to all Infidels and Hypocrites, that so long the Wrath of God doth ly on them, as theyJohn 20:21–23; Matthew 16:19; John 12:48 persist in their Wickedness, according to which Testimony of the Gospel God will judge them, as well in this life as in the life to come.

sp.speaker: Question 94:
sp.p: How is the Kingdom of Heaven opened and shut by Ecclesiastical Discipline?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: When according to the Commandments of Christ, they who in Name are Christians, but in their Doctrine and life shewRomans 12:7–9; 1 Corinthians 12:28 themselves Aliens from Christ, after they have been some time admonished, will not depart from their Error, Heresies, or Wickedness, are made known unto the Church; and if neither then they obey the Churches Admonition, are by the same Church kept from the Sacrament, and shut out by Authority received from Christ, from the CongregationMatthew 18:15–17; 1 Corinthians 5:3–5; 2 Thessalonians 3:14–15 or Church, and by God himself out of the Kingdom of Heaven. And again, if they profess and declare an amendment of life, nothing to the contrary being to be proved upon strict scrutiny and search, are again to2 Corinthians 2:6–7,10–11 be received in Love & Tenderness as Members of Christ and his Church.

div.head: 5. The third Part is of Man’s Thankfulness

sp.speaker: Question 95:
sp.p: Whereas we are delivered from all our Sins and Miseries without any Merit of ours, by the Mercy of God, only for Christ’s sake; for what cause are we to do good Works?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Because, after that Christ hath redeemed us with his Blood, he reneweth us also by his Spirit to the Image of himself, that we receiving so great Benefits,Romans 6:1,3; Romans 12:1–2; 1 Peter 2:5,9; 1 Corinthians 6:20 should shew our selves all our life time thankfull to1 Peter 2:12 God, and honour him; secondly that every one of us be2 Peter 1:10; Matthew 7:17–18; Galatians 5:22 assured of his Faith by his Fruit; and lastly, that by our good Conversation we may1 Peter 3:1–2; Matthew 5:16 win others to Christ.

sp.speaker: Question 96:
sp.p: Cannot they then be saved which be unthankful, and remain still careless in their Sins, and are not converted from their Wickedness to God?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: By no means; for as the Scripture beareth Witness, neither unchast Persons, nor Idolaters, nor Adulterers, nor Thievs, nor Covetous nor Drunkards, nor Slanderers, nor Robbers,1 Corinthians 6:9–10; Ephesians 5:5–6; 1 John 3:14–15 shall enter in to the Kingdom of God.

sp.speaker: Question 97:
sp.p: Of what Parts consisteth the Conversion of Man unto God?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: It consisteth of theRomans 6:4–6; Ephesians 4:22–24; Colossians 3:5,8–10; 1 Corinthians 5:7; 2 Corinthians 7:11 mortifying of the old Man, and a quickning of the new Man.

sp.speaker: Question 98:
sp.p: What is the mortifying of the old Man?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: To be truly and heartily sorry that thou hast offended God by thy Sins, and daily more and more hateRomans 8:13; Joel 2:13; Hosea 5:5 and eschew them.

sp.speaker: Question 99:
sp.p: What is the quickning of the new Man?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: True Joy in GodRomans 5:1; Romans 14:17; Isaiah 57:15 through Christ, and an earnest Desire to order thy Life according to God’s Will and toRomans 6:10–11; Galatians 2:20 do all good Works.

sp.speaker: Question 100:
sp.p: What are good Works?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Those only which are done by aRomans 14:23 true Faith, according1 Samuel 15:22; Ephesians 2:10 to God’s Law, and are1 Corinthians 10:31 referred only to his Glory, and not those which are imagined by us as seeming to us to be right and good, or whichDeuteronomy 11:32; Ezekiel 20:18–19; Isaiah 29:13; Matthew 15:9 are delivered and commanded by Men.

sp.speaker: Question 101:
sp.p: Which is the Law of God?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: The Decalogue, orExodus 20; Deuteronomy 5 ten Commandments.

sp.speaker: Question 102:
sp.p: How are these Commandments divided?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: IntoExodus 34:28; Deuteronomy 4:13; Deuteronomy 10:3–4 two Tables, whereof the former delivereth in four Commandments, how we ought to behave our selves towards God: the latter delivereth in six Commandments, what duties weMatthew 22:37–39 owe unto our Neighbours.

sp.speaker: Question 103:
sp.p: What is the Preface to the ten Commandments?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: I am JEHOVAH, the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the Land of Egypt, out of the House of Bondage.

sp.speaker: Question 104:
sp.p: What learn we from this Preface?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Three things: first he sheweth to whom the right of all Rule belongs, that is, to God himself. for I am (saith he) JEHOVAH. Secondly, he saith, he is the God of his People, that through the Promise of his Bountifulness he might allure them to obey him. Thirdly, he saith, which brought thee out of the Land of Egypt; as if he should say, I am he who have manifested my self unto thee and bestowed all those Blessings upon thee, therefore thou art bound to shew Thankfulness and Obedience unto me.Exodus 20:2

sp.speaker: Question 105:
sp.p: Do these things belong unto us?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: They do so, because they do figuratively comprehend and imply all the Deliverances of the Church; and further, also this was a Type of our wonderful Deliverance atcheived by Christ.

sp.speaker: Question 106:
sp.p: What is the first Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Thou shalt have no other Gods before me.

sp.speaker: Question 107:
sp.p: What doth God require in the first Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That as dearly as I tender the Salvation of my own Soul, so earnestly should I shun and sly1 Corinthians 6:9–10; 1 Corinthians 10:7,14 all Idolatry, Sorcery,Leviticus 19:31; Deuteronomy 18:11 Inchantments, Superstition, praying to Saints, or anyMatthew 4:10; Revelation 19:10; Revelation 22:8–9 other Creatures, and shouldJohn 17:3 rightly acknowledg the only and true God,Jeremiah 17:5 trust in himHebrews 10:36; Colossians 1:11; Romans 5:3–4; 1 Corinthians 10:10; Philippians 2:14 alone, submit and subject my selfunto him with all1 Peter 5:5–6 Humility, andPsalm 10:4; Isaiah 45:7; John 1:17 Patience, look for all good things from him alone, and lastly with the intire Affection of my HeartDeuteronomy 6:5; Matthew 22:37 love,Deuteronomy 6:2; Psalm 111:10 reverence, andMatthew 4:20 worship him, so that I am ready to renounce and forsake all Creatures ratherMatthew 5:29; Matthew 10:37–38 than to commit the least thing that may be against his Will.

sp.speaker: Question 108:
sp.p: What is Idolatry?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: It is in Place of that one God, or besides that one true God who hath manifested himself in his Word and Works, to make or imagin, and account any other thing wherein thou reposestPhilippians 3:19; Ephesians 5:5; Galatians 4:8; Ephesians 2:12; 1 John 2:23; John 5:23 thy Hope and Confidence.

sp.speaker: Question 109:
sp.p: What is the second Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Thou shalt make to thee no graven Image, nor the Likeness of any thing which is in Heaven above, or in the Earth beneath, nor in the Waters under the Earth: thou shalt not bow down to them, nor worship them, for I the Lord thy God am a jealous God, and visit the sins of the Fathers upon the Children, unto the third and fourth Generation of them that hate me, and shew Mercy to thousands of them which love me, and keep my Commandments.

sp.speaker: Question 110:
sp.p: What doth this second Commandment require?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That we should notDeuteronomy 4:15,&c; Isaiah 40:18,&c; Romans 1:23,&c; Acts 17:29 express or represent God by any Image or shape and figure, or worship him any otherwise then he hath commanded himself in1 Samuel 15:23; Deuteronomy 12:30,&c; Matthew 15:9 his Word to be worshipped.

sp.speaker: Question 111:
sp.p: May there then at all any Images or Resemblances of things be made?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: God neither ought, nor can be represented by any means: and for the Creatures, although it be lawful to express them, yet God forbiddeth notwithstanding their Images to be made or had, as thereby to worship or honour either them, or God by them:Exodus 23:24; Exodus 34:13–14,17; Numbers 33:52; Deuteronomy 7:5; Deuteronomy 12:13; Deuteronomy 16:22; 2 Kings 18:4

sp.speaker: Question 112:
sp.p: But may not Images be tolerated in Churches, which may serve for Books unto the common People?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: No, for ’tis not seemly that we should be wiser then God, who will have his Church to2 Timothy 3:16–17; 2 Peter 1:19 be taught by the lively preaching of his Word, and not withJeremiah 10:8,&c; Habakkuk 2:18–19 dumb Images.

sp.speaker: Question 113:
sp.p: What is the third Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Thou shalt not take the Name of the Lord thy God in vain; for the Lord will not hold him guiltless that taketh his Name in vain.

sp.speaker: Question 114:
sp.p: What doth God decree in the third Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That not only by cursingLeviticus 24:11,&c; Leviticus 19:12 or forswearing, but also byMatthew 5:37; James 5:12 rash swearing we should not use his Name despitefully, or unreverently, neither should by silence nor connivance be Partakers of these horrible Sins in others, but thatmissing we use the sacred and holy Name of God ever with great Devotion1 Timothy 2:8 and Reverence, that he may be worshipped and honoured by us with a true andRomans 2:24; 1 Timothy 6:1; Colossians 3:16–17 stedfast ConfessionMatthew 10:32 and Invocation of his Name; and lastly, in all our Words and Actions whatsoever.

sp.speaker: Question 115:
sp.p: Is it then so grievous a Sin by swearing, or banning, to take the Name of God in vain, as that God is also angry with them who in as much as in them lieth do not forbid or hinder it?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: SurelyLeviticus 5:1 most grievous: for neither is there any Sin greater, or more offending God, than the despiting of his sacred Name; wherefore also he would have this Sin to be punished with Death.Leviticus 24:15–16

sp.speaker: Question 116:
sp.p: May a Man swear religiously and lawfully, by the Name of God?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: He may when as either the lawful Magistrate exacteth it, or otherwise necessity requireth it: by this means the Faith and Truth of any Man, or thing to be ratified and established, whereby both the Glory of God may be advanced, and the safety of others procured: for this kind of Swearing isDeuteronomy 6:13; Deuteronomy 10:20; Isaiah 48:1; Hebrews 6:16 ordained by God’s Word, and therefore was wellGenesis 21:24; Genesis 31; Joshua 9:15,19; 2 Samuel 3:35; 1 Kings 1:29; Romans 1:9 used of the Fathers both in the old and new Testament.

sp.speaker: Question 117:
sp.p: Is it lawful to swear by Saints, or other Creatures?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: No, for a lawful Oath is an Invocation of God, whereby we desire that he, as the only searcher of Hearts, bear Witness unto the Truth, and will punish the Swearer if he2 Corinthians 1:23 wittingly swear falsely: but this HonourMatthew 5:3–4,34–36; James 5:12 agreeth to no Creature.

sp.speaker: Question 118:
sp.p: What is the fourth Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Remember that thou keep holy the Sabbath Day: six Days shalt thou labor, and do all that thou hast to do, but the seventh Day is the Sabbath of the Lord thy God, in it thou shalt do no manner of Work, Thou, nor thy Son, nor thy Daughter, thy Man-Servant, nor thy Maid-Servant, nor thy Cattel, nor the Stranger that is within thy Gates: for in six Days the Lord made Heaven, and Earth, the Sea, and all that in them is, and rested the seventh day, and hallowed it.

sp.speaker: Question 119:
sp.p: What are we taught by the fourth Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That one Day in seven be kept in the Worship of God, which under the old Testament was the last Day of the Week, but under the Gospel changed to the first Day of the Week, and this Lord’s Day to be spent in private and publique Devotion, as hearing the Word diligently, practising the Gospel-Sacraments zealously, and doing Deeds of Charity conscionably, and resting from servil Works, cases of necessity excepted, this being the laudable Practice of the holy Apostles, who best knew the Mind of Christ as to the time of Worship; neither do we find in all the new Testament, that any Gospel Church in the Apostles times did set any other Day apart solemnly to worship God, save the first Day: and well might they so do, for if Israel, the natural Seed of Abraham, was to keep the seventh Day, to keep up the Remembrance of their Deliverance out of temporal Bondage, how much more are we bound to keep the first Day in Remembrance of Christ’s Deliverance of us from eternal Bondage?Psalm 40:9–10; Acts 2:42,46; 1 Corinthians 14:19,29,31; Acts 20:7; 1 Corinthians 11:33; 1 Timothy 2:1–3,8–9; 1 Corinthians 14:16; 1 Corinthians 16:1–2; Isaiah 66:23; John 20:19–20; Revelation 1:10; Deuteronomy 5:15

sp.speaker: Question 120:
sp.p: What is the fifth Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Honour thy Father and Mother, that thy dayes may be long in the Land which the Lord thy God giveth thee.

sp.speaker: Question 121:
sp.p: What doth God enjoin us in the fifth Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That we yeild due honour, love, and faithfulness to our Parents, and so to all who bear Rule over us, andEphesians 6:1–2,5,&c; Colossians 3:20,22–24; Ephesians 5:22; Proverbs 1:8; Proverbs 4:1; Proverbs 15:20; Proverbs 20:20; Exodus 21:17; Romans 13:1 submit our selves with such obedience as is meet to their faithful Commandments and chastisements; and further also by that our patienceProverbs 23:22; Genesis 9:25; 1 Peter 2:18 we bear and suffer their manners, ever thinking with our selves that GodEphesians 6:4,9; Colossians 3:19,21; Romans 13:1; Matthew 22:21 will govern and guide us by their hand.

sp.speaker: Question 122:
sp.p: What is the sixth Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Thou shalt do no Murder.

sp.speaker: Question 123:
sp.p: What doth God exact in the sixth Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That neither in thought nor in gesture, much less in deed, I reproach, or hate, or harm, orMatthew 5:21–22; Genesis 9:6; Matthew 26:52 kill my Neighbour, either by my self, or by another, but cast awayEphesians 4:26; Romans 12:19; Matthew 18:35 all desire of revenge; furthermore, that I hurt not my self, nor cast my selfRomans 13:14; Colossians 2:23; Matthew 4:7 wittingly into any Danger. Wherefore also that Murther might not be committed, heGenesis 9:6; Exodus 21:14; Matthew 26:52; Romans 13:4 hath armed the Magistrate with the Sword.

sp.speaker: Question 124:
sp.p: But this Commandment seems to forbid Murther only?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: But in forbidding Murther, God doth further teach, that he hateth the Root, to wit,James 1:20; Galatians 5:20–21 Anger,Romans 1:29 Envy,1 John 2:9,11 Hatred, and Desire of Revenge, and1 John 3:15 doth account them all for Murther.

sp.speaker: Question 125:
sp.p: Is it enough then that we kill no Man, in such sort as hath been said?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: It is not enough; for when God condemneth Anger, Envy, Hatred, he requireth thatMatthew 22:39; Matthew 7:12 we love our Neighbour as our selves and that weRomans 12:10 use Humanity, Lenity,Ephesians 4:2; Galatians 6:1–2; Matthew 5:5; Romans 12:18; Matthew 5:7; Luke 6:36 Courtesie, Patience,Exodus 23:5 and Mercy towards him, andMatthew 5:45 turn away from him as much as we may whatsoever may be hurtful unto him; in a word, that we be so affected in Mind as that weRomans 12:20 stick not to do good also unto our Enemies.

sp.speaker: Question 126:
sp.p: What is the seventh Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Thou shalt not commit Adultery.

sp.speaker: Question 127:
sp.p: What is the meaning of the seventh Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That God hathLeviticus 18:27–28 in Execration all Turpitude and Filthiness, and therefore we alsoJude 22,23 must utterly hate, and detest it, and contrary-wife, live temperately, modestly, and1 Thessalonians 4:3–4 chastly, whether weHebrews 13:4; 1 Corinthians 7:4 live in holy Wedlock, or in single life.

sp.speaker: Question 128:
sp.p: Forbiddeth God nothing else in this Commandment but actual Adultery, and such kinds of uncleanness?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Yea, for seeing both our Body and Soul are the Temples of the Holy Ghost, God will have us to possess both in Purity and Holiness, and therefore Deeds,Ephesians 5:31; 1 Corinthians 6:18,20 Gestures, Words,Matthew 5:27–28 Thoughts, filthy Lusts, and whatsoever inticeth a Man unto these, all these GodEphesians 5:18; Job 31:1; Psalm 39:1 wholly forbiddeth.

sp.speaker: Question 129:
sp.p: What is the eighth Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Thou shalt not steal.

sp.speaker: Question 130:
sp.p: What doth God forbid in the eighth Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Not only those1 Corinthians 6:10 Thefts and1 Corinthians 5:10 Robberies, which the Magistrate punisheth, but by the name of Theft he comprehendeth whatsoever Evil, Crafts, Fetches, and Devices, whereby we seek after other Mens Goods, and indeavour with force, or with some shew of Right, toLuke 3:14; 1 Thessalonians 4:6 convey them over unto our selves; of which sort areProverbs 11:1; Proverbs 16:11 false Weights, false EllsEzekiel 45:9,&c; Deuteronomy 25:13,&c uneven Measures, deceitful Marchandize, counterfeit Coin,Psalm 15:5; Luke 6:35 Usury, or any other way or means of furthering our Estate, which God hath forbidden: to these we may add all1 Corinthians 6:10 Covetousness, and the manifold wast andProverbs 5:15 abusing of Gods Gifts.

sp.speaker: Question 131:
sp.p: What are those things which God here commandeth?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That to my Power, I help and further the Commodities and Profit of my Neighbour, and that I so deal with him as I would desire to be dealt with my self, and that I do my own Work plainly and faithfully, that I may thereby help others who are distressed with any need or Calamity.Matthew 7:12; Ephesians 4:28

sp.speaker: Question 132:
sp.p: What is the ninth Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Thou shalt not bear false Witness against thy Neighbour.

sp.speaker: Question 133:
sp.p: What doth the ninth Commandment exact?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That I bear noProverbs 19:5,9; Proverbs 21:28; Psalm 15:3 false Witness against any Man,missing neither falsifie any Man’s words, neither backbiteRomans 1:29–30 nor reproach any Man, norMatthew 7:1,&c; Luke 6:37 condemn any rashly, or unheard, but avoid, andJohn 8:44 shun with all carefulness all kind of Lies, and Deceipts, as the proper Works of the Devil, except I mean to stirProverbs 12:22; Proverbs 13:5 up against me the most grievous Wrath of God; and that in Judgments and other Affairs, I follow the Truth, and freely and constantlyEphesians 4:24–25 profess the matter as it indeed is, and moreover defend and increase as much as in me lieth, the good Name and Estimation of others.1 Peter 4:8

sp.speaker: Question 134:
sp.p: What is the tenth Commandment?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Thou shalt not covet thy Neighbours House, nor his Wife, nor his Servant, nor his Maid, nor his Ox, nor his Ass, nor any thing that is his.Exodus 20:17

sp.speaker: Question 135:
sp.p: What doth the tenth Commandment forbid?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That our Hearts be not at any time moved by the least Desire or Cogitation against any Commandment of God, butRomans 7:7,&c that continually and from our Heart we detest all Sin, and contrarily delight in all Righteousness.

sp.speaker: Question 136:
sp.p: But can they who are converted to God, perfectly observe, and keep these Commandments?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: No, but even the holiest Men as long they live, have only small Beginnings ofRomans 7:14–15; Ecclesiastes 7:22 this Obedience, yet so that theyRomans 7:22; James 2:10 begin with an unfeigned and earnest desire and endeavour to live not according to some only, but according to all the Commandments of God.

sp.speaker: Question 137:
sp.p: Why will God then have his Law to be so exactly and severely preached seeing there is no Man in this life able to keep it?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: First, That all our life time we more & more1 John 1:9; Psalm 22:5 acknowledg the great proneness of our Nature to Sin, and so much the moreRomans 7:24 greedily desire remission of Sins, and Righteousness in Christ. Secondly, That we be doing of this always, and always thinking of it, and so implore and crave of the Father the1 Corinthians 9:24,&c; Philippians 3:12–14 Grace of his Holy Spirit, whereby we may daily more and more be renewed to the Image and likeness of God, until at length after we are departed out of this life we may joyfully attain unto that Perfection which is promised unto us.

sp.speaker: Question 138:
sp.p: Wherefore is Prayer necessary for Christians?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Because it is the chief part of that thankfulness which God requireth of us, and also because God giveth them only his Grace and Holy Spirit, who with unfeigned gronings beg them continually of him and yeild him thanks for them.Matthew 7:7–8; Luke 11:9,13; Matthew 13:12; Psalm 50:15

sp.speaker: Question 139:
sp.p: What is required unto that Prayer which shall please God, and be heard of him?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That we ask of the only true God, who hathJohn 4:22,&c manifested himself in his Word, all things which he hath commanded to beRomans 8:26; 1 John 5:14 asked of him with a true affection and desire of our Heart, and through an inwardJohn 4:23–24; Psalm 145:18 feeling of our need andmissing misery cast our selves down prostrate in the presence of his Divine Majesty, andPsalm 2:11; Psalm 34:19; Isaiah 66:2 build our selves on this sure foundation, that we though unworthy, yet for Christ’s sake areRomans 10:14; Romans 8:15–16; James 1:6,&c certainly heard of God, even as he hathJohn 14:13; John 15:16; John 16:23; Daniel 9:17–18; Psalm 7:7–8; Psalm 143:1 promised us in his Word.

sp.speaker: Question 140:
sp.p: What are those things which he commandeth us to ask of him?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: All thingsMatthew 6:13; James 1:17 necessary both for Soul and Body, which our Lord Jesus Christ hath comprised in that Prayer, which himself hath taught us.

sp.speaker: Question 141:
sp.p: What Prayer is that?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Our Father which art in Heaven, hallowed be thy Name. Thy Kingdom come. Thy Will be done on Earth, as it is in Heaven. Give us this Day our daily Bread: And forgive us our Trespaffes, as we forgive them that trespass against us. And lead us not into Temptation, but deliver us from Evil: for thine is the Kingdom, the Power, and the Glory, for ever and ever, Amen.

sp.speaker: Question 142:
sp.p: Are Christians tied to this very Form of Prayer?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: We are not; our Lord here delivereth to his Church a brief Sum of those things which we are to ask of God, but yet Christ will have us also to descend unto specials, and to ask particular Benefits: for this Form prescribed is nothing else but a Set or Course of certain Heads or Generals, whereunto all Benefits both corporal and spiritual may be referred; but yet all particulars of Prayer must agree & correspond with this general Form, although we are not tied to this Form, as appeareth from James 1:5 where the Apostle exhorts the Saints, if any did lack Wisdom, they should ask of God, which giveth to all liberally, but these as touching the Words, are not in the Form of Prayer particularly expressed, though they are included. Besides, we have Examples of Prayer both in the old and new Testament, which are not the very Form here expressed, albeit, all they asked was comprehended in this Prayer, wherefore the Form of Prayer delivered unto us by Christ, is wholly a thing indifferent.

sp.speaker: Question 143:
sp.p: Why doth Christ teach us to call God our Father?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That presently in the very Entrance and Beginning of the Prayer, he might stir up in us such a Reverence, and Confidence of God as is meet for the Sons of God, which must be the ground and foundation of our Prayer, to wit, that God through Christ is made ourMatthew 7:9–10; Luke 11:11 Father, and will much less deny us these things which we ask of him with a true Faith, than our earthly Parents deny unto us earthly things.

sp.speaker: Question 144:
sp.p: Why is that added, which art in Heaven?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That weJeremiah 23:24; Acts 17:24–25,27 conceive not basely nor terrenely of God’s Heavenly Majesty, and also that weRomans 10:12 look for, and expect from his Omnipotency whatsoever things are necessary for our Soul and Body.

sp.speaker: Question 145:
sp.p: What is the first Petition?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Hallowed be thy Name; that is, grant us, first toJohn 17:3; Jeremiah 9:23–24; Jeremiah 31:33–34; Matthew 16:17; James 1:5; Psalm 119:105 know thee right, and worship, praise,Psalm 119:137–138; Luke 1:45–46,&c; Luke 1:68,&c; Psalm 145:8–9,17; Exodus 34:5–7; Psalm 143:1–2,5,10–12; Jeremiah 31:3; Jeremiah 32:18–19,40–41; Jeremiah 33:11,20; Matthew 19:17; Romans 3:3–4; Romans 11:22–23; 2 Timothy 2:19 and magnifie thy Almightiness, Goodness, Justice, Mercy and Truth, shining in all thy Works; and further also to direct our whole Life, Thoughts, Words, and Works to this end, that thy most Holy Name be not reproach’d by us, but rather bePsalm 115:1; Psalm 71:8 renowned with Honour, and Praises.

sp.speaker: Question 146:
sp.p: What is the second Petition?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Thy Kingdom come; that is, rule for us so by thy Word and Spirit, that we mayMatthew 6:33; Psalm 119:5; Psalm 143:10 humble and Submit our selves more and more unto thee. Also preserve and increase thyPsalm 122:6–7; Psalm 51:18; 1 John 3:8; Romans 16:20 Church, destroy the Works of the Devil, and all Power that lifteth up it self against thy Majesty; make all those Councils frustrate, and void, which areRevelation 22:17,20; Romans 8:22–23 taken against thy Word, until at length thou raign fully and perfectly, when thou shalt be all1 Corinthians 15:28 in all.

sp.speaker: Question 147:
sp.p: What is the third Petition?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Thy Will be done in Earth, as it is in Heaven. That is, grant that we, and all Men, renouncingMatthew 16:24; Titus 2:12 and forsaking our own Will, may readily, and without anyLuke 22:42 grudging, obey thy Will, which is only holy; and that so every one of us may1 Corinthians 7:24 faithfully perform that Duty and Charge which thou hast committed unto us, even as the blessed Angels doPsalm 103:20–21 in Heaven.

sp.speaker: Question 148:
sp.p: What is the fourth Petition?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Give us this Day our daily bread; that is, give unto us all things whichPsalm 145:15–16; Psalm 10:4; Matthew 6:25,&c are needful for this Life, that by them we may acknowledg and confess thee to be the only Fountain from whence all good thingsActs 17:27–28; Acts 14:16–17 flow; and all our Care and Industry, and even thine own Gifts to be unfortunate1 Corinthians 15:58; Deuteronomy 8:3; Psalm 27:13 and noisom unto us except thou bless them; wherefore grant that turning our Trust away from all Creatures, wePsalm 62:11 place and repose it in thee alone.

sp.speaker: Question 149:
sp.p: What is the fifth Petition?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Forgive us our Trespaffes, as we forgive them that trespass against us. That is, even for the Blood of Christ do notPsalm 51:1; Psalm 143:2 impute unto us most miserable and wretched sinners all our Offences, neither that Corruption which still cleaveth unto us, even as we also feel this Testimony of thy Grace in our Hearts, that we stedfastly purpose unfeignedly fromMatthew 6:14 our Hearts, to pardon and forgive all those who have offended us.

sp.speaker: Question 150:
sp.p: What is the sixth Petition?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: Lead us not into Temptation, but deliver us from Evil. That is, because we our selves, are so feeble and weak by Nature, thatJohn 15:5; Psalm 103:14 we cannot stand so much as one Moment or Instant, and our most deadly Enemies1 Peter 5:8; Ephesians 6:12 Satan, theJohn 15:19 World, and our ownRomans 7:23; Galatians 5:17 Flesh do incessantly oppugne and assault us, uphold thou us, and establish and strengthen us by the might of thy Spirit, that we may not in this spiritualMatthew 26:41; Mark 13:33 Combat yield as vanquished, but may so long stoutly withstand them, until at length1 Thessalonians 3:13; 1 Thessalonians 5:23 we get the full and perfect victory.

sp.speaker: Question 151:
sp.p: How concludest thou this Prayer?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: For thine is the Kingdom, the Power, and the Glory for ever. That is, we ask and crave all these things of thee, because seeing both thou art our King, and art Almighty, thou art both willing and ableRomans 10:11–12; 2 Peter 2:9 to give them all unto us; and these things we therefore ask, that out of them, not unto us, but unto thy holy Name all GloryPsalm 115:1; Jeremiah 33:8–9 may redound.

sp.speaker: Question 152:
sp.p: What meaneth this Particle, Amen?

sp.speaker: Answer:
sp.p: That the thing is sure, and out of doubt: for my Prayer is much more certainly heard of God, than I feel in my Heart that I unfeignedly2 Corinthians 1:20; 2 Timothy 2:13 desire the same.
